2306979:
Sakakabe

Sakakabe is a busy coastal town in Minkai. It is built on a favourable landing on an otherwise treacherous coastline.⁠⁠

Sakakabe is constructed on a series of steep, concentric terraces that extend from the port to the top of the hills, where the richest houses are built, while the lowest terraces lean on the ruins of a stone fortress built millennia ago. The ancient stone walls are adorned with reliefs of ancient warriors, but these images are now almost completely hidden by modern structures.⁠

The town is known for its entertainment district (or hanamachi), which is built on one of the highest terraces, centred on a large street called the Way of the Songbird.⁠
3361879:
Embassy Building

The Embassy Building in Magnimar is set aside for officially invited ambassadors from other countries. Many nations rejected the offer, but those who accepted exchanged functionaries and also receive lowered tariffs and increased trade. As of 4712 AR, the nations with representatives in Magnimar were Absalom, Andoran, Cheliax, Katapesh, Osirion, Qadira, Sargava (now known as Vidrian), Taldor, and Ustalav. Korvosa maintains offices here, but they are rarely used and remain empty most of the time. This two-story building is located in the city's Ordellia district.⁠
8373079:
Mallaru

Mallaru (pronounced mal-ya-ru)⁠ is the sole port city of the nation of Linvarre, which was previously the Taldan colony of Amanandar. The city is a recent expansion of the new nation's territory into lands formerly claimed by Shenmen and is located where the Ilushe River empties into the Sea of Ghosts.⁠
11126269:
Crystalrock

Crystalrock is a large, natural cavern located in the Mindspin Mountains of south-eastern Varisia near the banks of the Falcon River.⁠ It was discovered by the dwarves of Janderhoff who also call it the "Heart of the World". Within the cavern is an enormous crystal formation which hangs suspended from crystal threads. Dwarven elders have gathered here annually for centuries to watch the formation shake and give off a low pulse which can be felt for miles around. Lately the "heartbeat" has been occurring more rapidly, a fact which has caused the dwarves much concern; at the moment, it is aligned to the changes of the seasons.⁠⁠⁠

The cavern also gave its name to the Treaty of Crystalrock, signed here in 4472 AR between Janderhoff and the nearby Chelaxian city of Korvosa.⁠

27447949:
Tiantown

Tiantown is a neighborhood in the Foreign Quarter where most of the Tian Xia immigrants on Absalom reside. Although empires on that continent tend to be long-lasting, their fall results in great trauma for their inhabitants, who then move to Absalom and the most recent wave of migration came with the collapse of Lung Wa. Rival cultures and past enmities occasionally resurface, but the residents prefer the security of a familiar culture and language, blending with the more curious aspects of Absalom. Other unique residents include nagas, hobgoblins from Kaoling, and strange goblins never before seen in the Inner Sea.⁠

Shrike Cascade

The Shrike Cascade is a waterfall on the Shrike River situated about a dozen miles downriver from the Crooked Falls. Here, the Shrike drops from a slippery 50-foot-high cliff, which offers an excellent view of the surrounding landscape, but makes any travel by boat impossible.⁠⁠

52210429:
Cave of Darkfear

The Cave of Darkfear is actually an abandoned trapper's shack in Brinestump Marsh. Licktoad goblins used to challenge each other to see if they could go inside, because although there was no danger, the atmosphere was spooky for the little goblins.⁠
52648749:
Valorfoe

The cathedral-like, Ustalavic fortress of Valorforge at the Gap of Valballus in the Hold of Belkzen was one of the fortresses of the defensive barrier of Sunwall. When the Sunwall fell in 4237 AR the veteran soldiers of Lastwall retreated to a second line of defense but the Ustalavs of Valorforge didn't abandon their fortress in the face of invincible orc hordes and all within were slaughtered. Now known as Valorfoe, the abandoned castle is shunned by the orcs due to the shadowy terrors that lurk within.⁠⁠
56926969:
Ranulf's Keep

Ranulf's Keep was built by a member of the Ulfen Guard of the same name who protected his emperor until the latter died of natural causes. He was allowed to take whatever he could from the treasury and went north where he built his keep in the Tusk Mountains. He didn't realize the place was a dragon breeding ground, and after fighting an epic battle against one of these beasts, he defended the site for three decades and ordered an avalanche to be triggered to bury the keep after his death.⁠ Over the years, changing temperatures have allowed the entrance to one of its towers to remain open, although most of the structure is under snow, guarded by the kellid tribes of the region who followed this brave man.⁠
59482049:
Celwynvian

The ancient elven capital city of Celwynvian (pronounced sehl-WIN-vee-enn)⁠ sits amid the Mierani Forest in northern Varisia. Abandoned by the elves when they departed Golarion prior to the Earthfall, the city became overridden with drow, and was the site of one of the most vicious conflicts between the two elven races upon their return from Sovyrian. Taking considerable losses from the drow's evil tactics, the elves once again departed the city, and it remains empty and forbidden to this day.⁠

The elves of the Mierani Forest strictly prohibit outsiders from entering the city, under the guise of wanting to preserve it as a refuge from the rest of the world, but those more familiar with the region sense that the elves themselves avoid the city and are still involved in an ongoing war to reclaim it.⁠
59775869:
Boursonne

Boursonne was a town in Lastwall that was besieged and destroyed by the undead hordes of Tar-Baphon following his escape from Gallowspire in 4719 AR, as well as by cultists of Urgathoa. It was the target of a rescue and evacuation operation led by the Pathfinder Society by request of Second Sword Knight Aylunna Varvatos.⁠
81560569:
Sascha

Sascha, once called Ermalin, is a small Irriseni town in the Verge with a troubled past.⁠
82049049:
Redlake Fort

Redlake Fort was part of the Harchist's Blockade, defending the borders of Lastwall from its position in the Mindspin Mountains. The fort is built on a moat of the River Esk, whose algae give the water a reddish color, hence its name. Like other forts of the blockade, it fell to an orc siege in 4482 AR. In their desperation and hunger, its defenders were fed the flesh of their comrades by the fort's castellan to resist the attack, though it was in vain and these defeated guardians haunt the fort. In the following centuries, different forces have seized the fort, from orcs to hill giants and even ogres, with no one remaining for long due to the unsettling haunts that plague its inhabitants.⁠
87621499:
Halls of the Closed Fist

The Halls of the Closed Fist, located in the northeastern third level of Urgir in the Hold of Belkzen, serves as the headquarters of the Closed Fist, an elite unit that enforces the will of the city's overlord.⁠ Under the rule of Ardax the White-Hair, the Halls also effectively serve as his seat of government, as he leaves the Great Palace vacant⁠⁠ save for his predecessor Grask Uldeth's corpse.⁠
96535309:
Cettigne

Formerly an independent city-state, Molthune annexed Cettigne in 4708 AR when the city was beset by plague and famine. The nation installed Irina Klim, Molthune's youngest General Lord, as Cettigne's new ruler, but the locals continue to chafe at their new-found servitude. The traditional Free City Citizen Militia continues to protect the city independently of the General Lords. Friction between the locals and the national forces may soon lead to violence.⁠⁠⁠

Cettigne is built around four castles representing the various periods of its history; they are reflected on the city's flag, four white castles on a green field. A fifth castle is under construction, representing Molthuni rule.⁠

Cettigne has a small temple of Abadar.⁠
99409639:
Sisters of the Quill

The Sisters of the Quill is a congregation of women dedicated to preserving the written word, living in this two-story building. They are hired to translate books into other languages, and the business is run by Sister Masequa.⁠
103579689:
Dragonspring

The Dragonspring is located in the Darkmoon Plain in a thermal zone rich in copper, iron, and cobalt. Geysers abound in the region, spouting fiery water of varying colors depending on the mineral concentration. A dragon comes to the springs once or twice a year to bathe, then disappears, and no one has ever managed to speak to it or learn its name.⁠
104651439:
Parley Point

The surprisingly welcoming port of Parley Point is on the coast of the Garundi mainland region of the Shackles. It is a popular port of call for merchant captains travelling north, who often stop off here before braving the storms of the Eye of Abendego. It is renowned for its friendly citizens and fine inns (and brothels).

The Parley Point lighthouse warns passing vessels of the nearby reefs and dangerous surf. The crews of those vessels that do run aground are rescued by the town's fleet of galleys.

However, what the sailors fail to realise is that the town also has a second, false lighthouse further inland, that is sometimes used to fool captains into running aground. The citizens rescue these sailors in the same way as the others, but also surreptitiously make off with as much of their cargo as they can salvage.⁠
113540749:
Tomgruv

Tomgruv is located to the south of the Grungir Forest and to the north-east of Jol (the capital of Southmoor) in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. Today, it is officially ruled by Southmoor's Linnorm King Opir Eightfingers, but the local leaders will take control when they feel they can.⁠

The town is on the road between Jol and the Kopparberget mine. It is built around the entrance to an old abandoned mine. The locals who are mainly farmers and herders use the mine as a stronghold and storage facility. A few miners work on meager copper veins in the surrounding hills.⁠

Kobolds and other underground enemies dwell in the lower levels of the Tomgruv's abandoned mine but so far the residents have managed to keep the upper levels safe. Troll raiders find nothing worth outside the heavily fortified mine entrance.⁠

124130449:
Blackblood Cay

Blackblood Cay is a small port town on Shark Island in the Shackles. It is located on a small hidden inlet of the island and was founded by Free Captain Simeon the Vain in 4703 AR. The port now hosts ten more pirate captains, while Simeon remains lord of Blackblood Cay. The town features berths along the wharf for only six vessels at a time.
126906269:
District Courthouse

The District Courthouse in Eastgate has a reputation for the compassion shown by its judges and prosecutors, which makes sense given the close-knit nature of the district, but some of its sentences border on negligence. Samel Maleagant transfers the city's most depraved criminals to this courthouse, exploiting the situation to secure lighter sentences for his clients.⁠

133126969:
Lissalan Temple

The Lissalan Temple in the Wyvern Mountains is one of several temples dedicated to the rune goddess in Varisia. During Earthfall, the entrance was blocked by boulders, and for millennia, no one disturbed the location until modern cultists of the goddess discovered that it contained tokens capable of leading them to where Krune lay, awaiting awakening.⁠ In 4713 AR, pathfinders following the cultists' trail found the temple and obtained some tokens.⁠
135834649:
Bronze Hook

Bronze Hook is a small trading town located in the foothills of northwestern Katapesh's Brazen Peaks, just a short distance north of the Pale River. Once a stop on a now-defunct caravan route from Ipeq to Solku, the town no longer makes the profits it once did ferrying goods and passengers across the river and charging tolls for the use of the Hook Ford. Since the trade route fell into disuse, the people of Bronze Hook have learned to survive off of what little trade trickles along the old road or the river. With their town's coffers always in mind, the local constabulary has increasingly turned a blind eye as slavers, smugglers, and traders of exotic creatures from the Brazen Peaks bring their goods through the town, despite the moral implications and frequent disturbances that come with them.⁠
138122989:
Vilelock

Vilelock is a shady, lawless settlement on the Shark Island in the Shackles. As expected, gory brawls, lurking cutpurses, and casual murders are frequent in town.

A thriving market in Vilelock specializes in the acquisition and sale of exotic poisons and alchemical substances outlawed in the more civilized nations of the Inner Sea region.

The town changes overlords often but its current overlord is Nisia Gbele, the Mwangi captain of the frigate Bloody Cudgel.⁠
144151789:
Ecru

Ecru was a mining village in the Hollow Hills specializing in extracting valuable sulfur from nearby mines, which was sold at a good price to neighboring towns. The town fell under the control of the Ironfang Legion in 4717 AR and they used it as a base for transporting supplies throughout the region.⁠
145850109:
House of Lords

The House of Lords is a municipal building of Magnimar's city government in Varisia. Located in the wealthy Alabaster District, the temple-like structure holds offices for each of the city's seven great aristocratic families. Members of the public can appeal to the representatives of each of these families here in order to air grievances, ask for favors, or otherwise deal with the needs of the citizens at large. Magnimar's lesser aristocratic families do not have permanent offices here, but may rent them for a small fee should they so choose.⁠
150540169:
Baphon's Fall

Baphon's Fall is a waterfall approximately 1,800 feet high, colloquially named after the belief that Aroden defeated Tar-Baphon in the area. The waterfall's water originates from the Whispering River, which carries the void energy produced by the storms surrounding The Three Furies. As a result, the water is harmful to living beings, and the vegetation near the falls is blackened and lifeless.⁠

158069929:
The Old Light

The Old Light is the most visible landmark of the western Varisian town of Sandpoint. It is believed to have been a lighthouse during the ancient Thassilonian empire, though much of the structure has crumbled over the ages.⁠
164884249:
Stockyards

The Stockyards is Kaer Maga's biggest and most well-known place to buy, sell, or rent beasts. Located in the Varisian city's public Downmarket district, it deals predominantly in horses and aurochs to serve as mounts or draft animals. These creatures are generally sold by (or stolen from) local Shoanti tribes of the Storval Plateau. The Stockyards occasionally does business in more exotic fauna, captured abroad or in the nearby Cinderlands. These include smaller animals, such as the hyena-like bush tigers, canine kominkas, and cinder wolves, generally sold as guard animals or pets, but also the occasional megafauna brought by orcs from the Hold of Belkzen. The latter are generally not allowed into the city unless under heavy restraints, for fear that they will break loose and wreak havoc.⁠
188232479:
Laughing Wave Inn

The Laughing Wave Inn is the oldest surviving in on the mainland of Korvosa, one of the only buildings to survive the Shoanti attack known as the Second Battle of Mainshore during 4439 AR. Named after the nickname of Keyra Palin, one of the heroes of early Korvosa, the Laughing Wave Inn is located in the North Point district. The inn shows its age with sagging balconies and a hundred other signs of the centuries of wear and tear it has endured. Still the inn is popular, especially with visitors to Korvosa, due to the Barbarian Princess, a Shoanti ghost who haunts the Laughing Wave and is said to appear regularly on both solstices, as well as the night of the Riverwind Festival.⁠
197501239:
Genzei

Genzei, the City of Lanterns, is the capital of the Ushinawa Isles. It was established nearly two centuries ago, when samurai patriarch Tanagowu Useme conquered the islands.

The fiercely independent samurai and his rowdy followers fought the murderous kuru natives who populated the stony Ghol-Gani ruins that dotted the island. The bloody fighting lasted one month and, at the end, every kuru was put to the sword. The warriors and the Tian-Min sailors and servants who accompanied them established the new, limestone town of Genzei.

The settlers went to great efforts to erase any signs of the original Ghol-Gani builders, painting over the depictions of cannibalism and bloody alien rituals and removing the limestone carvings portraying their ravenous gods.⁠
205974749:
Riekamesto

Riekamesto is a small town on Glacier Lake in the Irriseni province of Thronehold that has seen quite a bit of recent trouble.⁠

As of 4713 AR, the Cold Sisters had recently discovered that Baroness Urszula and 13 of her councilors had been cheating Whitethrone by hiding tax revenues. Cold Sisters viciously killed these councilors by throwing them from the top floor of the Council House. Urszula was instead buried alive in a great brass coffin wrapped with bands of iron inscribed with strange sigils. They placed the coffin in the center of the town, and as of six months later Urszula's desperate cries and frantic pounding continued from within.⁠

Sister Arminaela was temporarily made the town's administrator, and achieved hard work and discipline from the peasants and increased tax revenues.⁠
208240159:
Gruankus

The massive rune-covered wheel of Gruankus lies half-buried on the shore of the Varisian Gulf. Presumably a Thassilonian artifact, its original purpose remains unknown, much the same as the Cyphergate in Riddleport to its east. It was the location of the signing of the Treaty of Gruankus between the pirates of Riddleport and the leaders of Magnimar at some point after 4607 AR, ostensibly to reduce the danger of piracy to traders travelling the Varisian Gulf.⁠⁠⁠
216860969:
Crossfen

Crossfen is a Nirmathi village in the Fangwood near the Lastwall border⁠ and a mile-wide wetland. Of the settlements inside the Fangwood, Crossfen is one of the few capable of supporting cattle that feed on thick-growing sedge.⁠

The wetlands host boggards and will-o'-wisps known to claim visitors and villagers who attempt to cross it at night.⁠
218095069:
Crackspike

Crackspike is a formation of prospectors' bones in Devil's Perch, erected as both a warning and summer roost by the area's native Windspire tribe of strix around 4690 AR.⁠ The Chelaxian provincial authorities attempted to secure Crackspike around 4711 AR as a base for mining silver from Sorvus's Strike about two miles northwest of Crackspike; the strix subsequently burned the settlement to the ground.⁠
238759869:
Irogath Monastery

Irogath Monastery is located at the foot of the Mindspin Mountains, where Kuthite monks reside and train in ascetic scarification. The complex is designed to facilitate this discipline, with undecorated corridors, beds without pillows, and short benches—everything constructed to help the monks contemplate the suffering of life.⁠

Those pilgrims wishing to enter the inner chambers must obtain the approval of Mistress Merinda the Striped, who is said to be able to discern a person's devotion to Zon-Kuthon simply by looking into their eyes. The trials to be endured in these inner chambers are agonizing, and the few who succeed never speak of what they gained upon completing the journey.⁠
246365909:
Lumber Consortium Camp

As of 4708 AR, the Lumber Consortium Camp in Andoran's Darkmoon Vale was the lumber cartel's main camp in the region.⁠⁠ It specializes in harvesting copses of valuable duskwood.⁠⁠
249749419:
House of Guile

The House of Guile is a gallery in Eastgate where Parsin Guile exhibits his works—some artistic, others more practical, featuring mechanical designs in wood—to the general public. The commercial side is managed by his wife, Hilenda Guile. The building's facade features over 30 different types of wood sourced from the Isle of Kortos, some of which have been extinct for centuries.⁠
264449689:
Numijaan

Numijaan is the mostly ruined capital of Wanshou in Tian Xia. A pale shadow of its former self, Numijaan once boasted more than 170,000 residents before a series of disastrous storms and the emergence of the elder kraken Zhanagorr laid waste to it.⁠
266177039:
Nystra

Nystra is a ghost-town in the far-eastern reaches of the River Kingdoms. Once a thriving community centered around the cultivation and production of the fine silk produced by the insectoid silk gargoyles, or silkgoyles, its inhabitants were totally wiped out in a revenge plot by the Taldan druid Tharl Grimull in 4664 AR.⁠⁠
285632159:
Ajitesh Valley

Ajitesh Valley is a holy site in the north-western corner of the Divine Garden region of the Impossible Kingdoms of Vudra. The valley is a natural elephant graveyard where the beasts go to die.⁠

In 4465 AR, the Vile Prince Rajput Shivji Shashibhushan, a powerful necromancer, violated this sacred site to harvest its vast supply of bone and ivory and build undead known as rajput ambari. He also used the materials for his blasphemous Palace of Ivory and Bone.⁠
295673889:
Postern

The Postern Gate, or simply the Postern, is the eastern gate of Absalom. It is the smallest of the city's gates, only 50 feet high and 40 feet wide, and the only one that is normally kept closed and locked. It is a defensive building designed by Aroden and made of thick stone with balconies, and is used mainly to get goods to and from the Starwatch Keep.

The gate was often the focus of siege attacks, and was breached during the Siege of Prophets even if the enemy forces proved unable to penetrate the city. A carved stone set in the last hall within the Postern commemorates the deepest point the enemy reached. The Postern Gate also serves as the headquarters of Eastgate's district guard, the Post Guard.⁠
305372589:
Stoneshield House

Stoneshield House serves as the headquarters for the Graycloaks, the district watch of the Ascendant Court district of Absalom. Stoneshield House is named in honour of Dunarr Stoneshield, a former captain of the Graycloaks who is treated almost like a secular saint by serving members of the Graycloaks. The Graycloaks themselves are all atheists, allowing them to police the countless religions that call the Ascendant Court home with a sense of fairness, uninfluenced by any faith in the gods. They are currently led by Runewulf the Unbeliever, who lives within Stoneshield House. The building of Stoneshield House is understated in form, particularly when compared with the endless ostentatious temples and shrines within the district. Still, the Stoneshield House has its own imposing, ominous air to it. The Graycloaks are called on to deal with strange and powerful threats, and who knows what they have locked away within their headquarters.⁠
306028189:
Tern Hill

Tern Hill is a cavern in the Verduran Forest that collapsed, creating an open, roofless space. Tall trees surround the hill, their canopies blocking the view, while their thick roots are visible inside the cavern. Several tunnels connect the cavern's chambers, making it an easily defensible location.⁠

The Rootweft Lodge used the cavern as a base of operations during the Wildwood Revolt, taking advantage of its defensive strengths.⁠
311925259:
Pleasure Salon of Calistria

Elves and aiuvarins are common among the temple prostitutes of the Pleasure Salon of Calistria in the Ascendant Court district of Absalom.⁠ Elves are otherwise relatively uncommon in Absalom, mostly consisting of adventurers or outcasts; more common are their half-elven descendants.⁠ Although Calistria's priests play a significant role in the operations of the temple, the Pleasure Salon is managed by the ranking sacred prostitute, Dyrianna of House Avenstar.⁠

333214789:
Vellumis

Vellumis was the oldest and largest city in the nation of Lastwall, and remains the largest bastion of the Knights of Lastwall in the Gravelands since the nation was destroyed by Tar-Baphon in 4719 AR.⁠

Situated on the shores of Lake Encarthan, it served as the port of embarkation and debarkation for soldiers traveling in and out of the country on their way to keep watch over the terrors of Ustalav and the Hold of Belkzen,⁠ then as the evacuation point for refugees fleeing the nation after 4719 AR.⁠⁠
350708279:
Bodie's Haunt

Bodie's Haunt was once a settlement in the River Kingdoms, in what is now called the Protectorate of the Black Marquis.

Up until 4707 AR, it was home to one of the three rival Marquises vying for control of the Pirate Pact. However, in that year Urdal Bazzak arranged for the inhabitants to be slaughtered by Numerian soldiers as his first step to gaining control of the Protectorate.

Today, the town is a ruin haunted by the angry souls of the slain pirates.⁠
351549119:
Ferny

The village of Ferny is the largest settlement of shoonies in the Swardlands of the Isle of Kortos.⁠
351558649:
Annexa Palanthea's Fishy Menagerie

Located in the Docks section of Katapesh Annexa Palanthea's Fishy Menagerie is a unique wharf-side attraction that is part museum, part aquarium. For only a single silver piece, anyone can enter and see live fish from all of Golarion's seas, including live piranha from the Mwangi Expanse, a variety of squids and octopuses, and an overweight bunyip. The stuffed attractions are even more impressive, including several intelligent underwater dwellers like ulat-kinis, sedacthies, athamarus, and merfolk. The stuffed collection also includes larger creatures such as a water naga, a young kraken, a mighty alghollthu master, and even an enormous mottled worm.

The Fishy Menagerie is run by Annexa Palanthea, an expert on aquatic life who is said to pay very well for any new and interesting samples—though due to her expansive knowledge, it takes a rare specimen to qualify as either. Annexa sometimes even funds expeditions to search the Inner Sea for new specimens; this interest puts her in competition with the operators of Jexler & Young Salvage Company and Deep Sea Exploration and Retrieval.⁠
355215419:
Tamrivena

The county town of Tamrivena is located in the western Ustalavic county of Canterwall, one of the Palatinates, in close proximity to the unsettling Shudderwood. The county of Tamrivena was one of the first to declare its independence from traditional rule after nearby Lozeri did so in 4670 AR, replacing its hereditary ruler with a Palatine Council in a bloodless coup and changing its name to Canterwall.⁠⁠
360120029:
Tarheel Promenade

Tarheel Promenade gives its name to the district, and this street is completely blackened as if a black river had flowed through the area and frozen solid. Many magical shops are located there, and those who look at the street for a while can see the river flowing, which should be physically impossible.⁠
360471649:
Downpour

Downpour is a small fishing town on Tempest Cay island in the Shackles. It was founded to take advantage of the plentiful fish that once made their way up and down the Bluehook River during spawning season. Since the cruel catoblepas Gruzugr made its home in the river, the waters have been poisoned and the fish are gone. The residents survive by harvesting the numerous nearby clam colonies.⁠
361881069:
Avennara

Avennara is an elf village located near the western edge of the Fierani Forest halfway between the settlements of Riverspire and Erages.⁠ An elf gate within the village opens to a large number of other gates around Golarion.⁠ This gate has been activated thanks to the Godsrain connecting it to unknown locations, with strange animals that have come though causing havoc and bounties for their capture have been place on them.⁠

The Lantern Bearers, an elven secret society that hunts the drow, use a site close to the gate as their main meeting place.⁠
368561869:
Oyster Cay

The port of Oyster Cay is in the Mainland region of the Shackles.

It is currently suffering as two Free Captains vie for control of the port, namely Havalas Grudd and his estranged lover Wide Olga.⁠

391023929:
Gillamoor

Gillamoor is a village in Isger on the edge of the Chitterwood. It managed to survive the destruction of the Goblinblood Wars but has now fallen to what is being called the Gillamoor Plague.

According to the usually fearless caravan guards of the Mercenary League, many of the villagers have been transformed into ravenous disease-carrying zombies.⁠ The village is under quarantine by order of the Isgeri army, and its leaders secretly hope that the steward's 5,000 gold piece reward for eliminating the undead plague will convince outsiders to cleanse the town for them. A few of the village's inhabitants are still believed to be alive, trying to last out the siege in heavily barricaded homes.⁠
400972669:
Little Lirgen

Little Lirgen is a neighborhood in the Foreign Quarter where the diaspora of the fallen nation of Lirgen gathers, and most of them maintain their nation's astronomical traditions. Mosaics of stars fill the streets, painted like the night sky, and although in the first few years after the Eye of Abendego opened they hoped the storm would dissipate, they are increasingly uncertain about whether to remain culturally separate from the rest of Absalom or assimilate. The death of prophecy has rendered many of their stargazing rituals and artifacts obsolete, and a feeling of emptiness fills the hearts of these residents. The neighborhood is also where the city's lizardfolk population gathers, with inns offering live fish to eat, hot showers to sleep in, and lights that provide solar warmth in the winter.⁠

They are informed by the residents there that they have to wait in the town until a Caretaker seeks them out, when one of the Eyes is willing to give an audience. Rikhist

623583239:
Ghasterhall

Ghasterhall is an infamous library located in Virlych. It is also known as the Palace of Travesties.⁠ Although a place of retained knowledge, Ghasterhall displays horrific methods of storing information. Ghasts possessing oracular power stalk the blood-splattered halls and dead victims are nailed to the walls, used for necromantic experimentation.⁠

Ghasterhall has been described as an inverted tower-pit, serving as both prison and library. The awakened demilich Geir acts as head researcher for Tar-Baphon, establishing himself as curator of the massive library, laboratory, and prison.⁠⁠ Although a horde of undying scholars still possess tremendous accumulated knowledge, only Geir continues with his endless experimentation on esoteric matters.⁠

Ambition for dark knowledge waned with the imprisonment of the Whispering Tyrant,⁠ but after his escape in 4719 AR, Tar-Baphon sought Geir's aid in developing a method of either transforming the orcs of Belkzen into an undead army or destroying them.⁠

For a time, Lucimar the Lich-Wolf sequestered himself in the prison-library.⁠ By 4711 AR, Ghasterhall served as headquarters for the Whispering Way.⁠

Lady's Light

Golden Scarab

The Scarab is perhaps the most famous gambling hall in the city, and its owner, Krebble-Jeggle adds new games to the hall at a breakneck pace. The selection of games includes roulette, cards, darts, dice games, and more exotic (and disreputable) games can be found upstairs in the Upper Hall.

The basement of the building is the home of the bloodiest games in all of Golarion: Mig-a-Mug-Tug, Hatch-a-Catch, Knivesies, and Killgull for example. Games involving undead are common as well; Zombie Melee, for example, is a "to the death" game where necromancers pit teams of zombies against each other.

Interestingly, there are no pit fights or duels to be found in the basement of the Golden Scarab. This is because the Pactmasters have granted the Guild of Gladiators sole rights to these sorts of sports.⁠

These tributes can consist of anything ranging from treasure to livestock to slaves. The dromaar alchemist Rzonca the Clever resides in a small hut in the shadow of the Covenant Rock and acts as the agent of the red dragons of Raschka-Tor.⁠⁠

702894329:
Pillars of Kreth

The Pillars of Kreth are located on the plains just west of the Flood Road in northern Belkzen. The Pillars are a series of eleven dolmens—massive vertical standing stones topped with flat lintels. The site was discovered by the orc Kreth but the orcs are superstitious by nature and they have never revisited the Pillars of Kreth since then. The first ten dolmens are each between 8 and 9 feet in height, 3 feet wide and 2 feet thick. The linels are 3 feet thick, overhanging the stones beneath them by approximately a foot on all sides. The easternmost dolmen is only around 4 feet high. The stones seem to have been worked by primitive hand tools and contain numerous symbols and pictograms that correspond to no known language. Some of the symbols are clearly stars, comets, and planets. The eleven dolmens forms an irregular tunnel that once a year aligns with the red planet Akiton. During this time the sky above the Pillars turns strange colors, and a vibration can be felt from half a mile away. As the vibrations become stronger, a torus of churning auroral light rises a mile above the site and a pulse of energy passes through the first ten dolmens and strikes the top of the easternmost one. Anything on top of the last dolmen dissapears for ever. ⁠

Pathfinders who have studied the Pillars of Kreth believe that they could be a kind of interplanetary transportation device, similar to the Doorway to the Red Star in the Mwangi Expanse or the Maze of the Open Road in Galt.⁠

Swift Dolphin Warehouse

Swift Dolphin Warehouse is a failed, boarded-up warehouse in Magnimar's Underbridge district.⁠ Unknown to most is that under this site, the Midnight Dawn operate a drug parlor serving midnight milk.⁠
961713019:
Wachail Estate

The Wachail Estate serves as the residence of the decaying noble family led by Lord Navvem. It was raided in 4720 AR after he refused to free his slaves when the practice was outlawed. The stone house resembles a fortress, and since then the family has sought alliances with all manner of unsavory individuals in an attempt to recapture their former glory.⁠
963034579:
Reanpharos

Reanpharos, or Reanphoros, also called the City Between Two Rivers, is the capital of the city-state of Pol-Reanpharos in the Iblydan archipelago. It is home of Chinostes, the Fallen Blade, an Iblydan hero-god of tragedy and sacrifice.⁠
968282909:
Gallery of Innovation

The Gallery of Innovation is the Brigh temple in Absalom run by the impassive High Priestess Flindish Tanwhirl. Followers from all over the Inner Sea come to the temple, which is filled with engineers, blacksmiths, and metalworkers who push their skills to the limit working in the workshops inside. Constant classes and seminars are given by the clergy on the functions of inventions or new ideas that can be put into practice.⁠

Plains of Night

The Plains of Night is a ranch in the Atteran Ranches that is not run by the Atteran family or other regular ranchers. The ranch raises horses efficiently, and this ability has earned the respect of the locals, although there is suspicion surrounding the ranch workers, who are mostly foreigners.⁠

It turns out that these suspicions are correct, as the owner, Etrixia Star-Touched, was a cleric of Desna, and her ranch serves as a base of operations for rebels. 995539409:
House of Whips

The House of Whips is a shop catering to sadomasochists, run by a woman who wears red silks and is an open secret to be a succubus who drains the energy of her more healthy customers through the lashing of her whips. She uses magic to control the minds of her "employees" and sometimes struggles to resist acquiring a beautiful new toy that enters her establishment.⁠
1005163799:
Cindra's Exotic Pets

Cindra's Exotic Pets is a shop that promises to sell the most diverse animal species from the Inner Sea, including monkeys from the Mwangi Expanse, dinosaurs from Mediogalti Island, snakes from the Mana Wastes, crocodiles from Osirion, toads from the Sodden Lands, white ravens from Irrisen, wolves and foxes from Nirmathas, and much more.⁠
1007219369:
Brine

The Brine is an imposing stone prison house located in the Puddles district in Absalom. Lady Seichya of House Tevineg serves as the prison's head warden.⁠

Ever since the regular flooding of the district, The Brine has ensured a slow but certain death for the criminals within. The holding pens is usually soaked with at least a foot of water from the flooding, but also raw sewage washes in from time to time, typically resulting in outbreaks of filth fever and general sickness.

Although the guards use elevated catwalks to stay out of the muck, the prisoners below frequently are forced to stand, sit and sleep in the foul waters.⁠

Especially important individuals are sent to Black Whale prison.

The Salt Cartel fills its stocks of slaves from prisoners fraudulently collected from the Brine.⁠
1015659159:
Vigil's Hope

Vigil's Hope, located in the Precipice Quarter of Absalom, is the headquarters of the Knights of Lastwall and serves as an embassy for the exiled leadership of the destroyed nation of Lastwall. Watcher-Lord Ulthun II resides in Vigil's Hope, from where he coordinates the organization's diplomatic and fundraising activities.⁠
1015862829:
Avrossi

Avrossi is a hamlet located 50 miles south of Mechitar, filled with estates granted to loyal servants of Gebbite leaders. From this unassuming place, Avrossi's mayor Furghol Rennold has been plotting against his own family for decades. Its population, consisting primarily of human wizards and clerics of Urgathoa as well as bodak, mohrg and ghoul wizards, employs mindless skeletons and zombie as field workers, and regularly receives human chattel from Corpseblight.⁠

Uqtaal Necropolis

The Uqtaal ​​Necropolis is located near the Path of Aganhei, on the section of the Wall of Heaven that faces the Crown of the World. Centuries ago, followers of Desna built this necropolis, but their descendants were not as devoted to the goddess, eventually following the malevolent god Fumeiyoshi. They began attacking anyone who approached them, causing several Erutaki tribes to unite against them. Currently, a tribe of yeti led by Bormurg uses the caverns as their home.⁠
1029011989:
Pashow

Pashow is the smallest of Thuvia's five allied city-states. It lies in the barren south of the country, in a location conveniently close to the Citadel of the Alchemist but lacking in natural resources. It was ruled by Emir Guldis until very recently.⁠ The city's inhabitants are known for their magical talents and revere Nethys as their patron deity. They use magic to help compensate for the harshness of the local environment.⁠
1038391769:
Baifen

Baifen serves as a central gathering place for the various small Tapestry People communities within the lands of the Szaezan Crags leased by Hao Jin. The day-to-day running of the town is done collectively by about a hundred families.

Baifen is a popular holiday destination because of its many attractions, such as public theater performances, hot spring bathhouses, and night markets filled with delicious foods. Historians and adventurers are also attracted to the area, with the hope that one of the Tapestry People can help solve ancient riddles or provide otherwise lost historical knowledge.⁠
1042014509:
Lavieton

Lavieton is a small Andoran fishing village on the Inner Sea coast, approximately 250 miles southeast of the city of Augustana.⁠ The finest fish in all of the Inner Sea are said to be caught here, and the fishmonger at the Sign of the Blue Sail is known throughout the Inner Sea region.⁠⁠ The best fishing is from midsummer through early autumn, after which Waldry Quence and the other workers at the Sign of the Blue Sail smoke the fish and prepare them for export. The houses of Lavieton are generally small and of wattle and daub construction, and sit on sandy dunes on the top of a seaside bluff.⁠
1044539669:
Troglodyte Caves

The Troglodyte Caves are located within the Lady's Cape and are named after the xulgath tribe that lives there, the Children of Zevgavizeb. The caverns connect to a tunnel system that provides access to the Lady's Light, though few besides the xulgath could use them due to the foul odor that permeates all the caves.⁠
1047498939:
Nightways Gate

The Nightways Gate and the Night Road are named for linking Kintargo to its shadowy northern neighbour of Nidal via the scholastic district of Villegre. The gate and road form an awkward but necessary trade route, as due to Kintargo's distance from Cheliax's central heartlands, goods from Nidal are often cheaper.

When Kintargo was under Chelaxian rule, this route also granted the fell influence of Nidalese culture another inroad into Cheliax.⁠ After Kintargo and Ravounel won their independence from Cheliax in 4716 AR, Lord Mayor Jilia Bainilus has engaged in active diplomacy with Nidal.⁠
1049445439:
Westpool

The small port towns of East Rikkan and Westpool, located north of Westcrown in Cheliax, are known collectively as the Rikkan Ports. These settlements house large numbers of merchants who trade goods up and down the River Adivian, and as of 4709 AR (prior to the abolition of slavery in Cheliax) also housed the numerous slaves required to operate the Stavian Arches and portage stations. Westpool is larger due to the presence of the Arch.

Since 4674 AR, Chelaxian forces frequently occupy the town looking for rebels and traitors. The current mayor of Westpool, Vismargrave of the Adivian Falling Tibalt Khrocini openly engages in politics and has gained much power and many enemies by controlling the transport route to Lake Sorrow and the capital Egorian.⁠
1056749699:
Eongman Bog

Eongman Bog is the largest enclave of dokkaebi in Tian Xia, with few human residents. The settlement hosts an annual festival where dokkaebi engage in kimchi-eating competitions.⁠
1064396419:
Pyramid of Doom

The Pyramid of Doom is a site in southern Osirion. It is located to the west of the Salt Hills.⁠
1067958709:
Olfden

Olfden is a large Andoren town located in the nation's Darkmoon Vale region, halfway between Falcon's Hollow and Oregent, and only a few miles away from Adamas, headquarters of the Diamond Regiment.
1070216799:
Serenity's Copse

Serenity's Copse is a community of dryads who live in a grove deep in Cheliax's Anferita Wood.⁠
1071170349:
Nine Walls

Nine Walls is a heavily defended nation of Matanji orcs located in the Mwangi Expanse. Its name is derived from its nine concentric cities, each ringed in tall, fortified, hexagonally shaped walls.⁠⁠ Despite being beset by demons throughout its existence, the inner sanctums of Nine Walls are among the safest locations of the Expanse as well as some of the most cultured centers of orc civilization in the Inner Sea region.⁠⁠
1072962599:
Pit of Raugsmauda

The Pit of Raugsmauda is located on Motaku Isle in the Shackles. It was the former subterranean lair of the infamous sorcerer Raugsmauda.⁠

It was assumed that Raugsmauda was gone forever but, in 4512 AR, a group of adventurers descended into the Pit of Raugsmauda and discovered the sorcerer, now transformed into a vicious lich. The adventurers fought Raugsmauda, who fled westward and eventually settled on a small, uninhabited, cave-riddled volcanic isle that now has the name of Raugsmauda's Reach.⁠

The upper levels of the Pit have long been plundered over the years, but much of the massive dungeons in the Pit's cavernous depths remain unexplored, and potentially hold Raugsmauda's treasures and horrors.⁠
1073089289:
Crimsonlight Dig

The Crimsonlight Dig is one of the few archaeological sites in Kahlehlin. So far, the dig has unearthed ruins, an obsidian menhir, several glowing red stones, and more.⁠
1078306179:
The Uskheart

The Uskheart is the central redoubt of the infamous Nidalese circle of druids called the Shades of the Uskwood. Located in the southern Uskwood, the Shades have recently uncovered a disturbing life form known as the hive. These creatures consume and transform everything they encounter, and they seem to be outside the natural order of Golarion. Despite their uniqueness, they are not extraplanar or supernatural in origin and refer to themselves by an unpronounceable Aklo word.⁠
1080633959:
Thanegraves

The Thanegraves, located in western Wintercrux in Irrisen, are the final resting place of the Djurstor Confederacy thanes. Two boreal ogre tribes claim the hilly stretch, which is dotted with burial mounds and tombs and largely forgotten by the area's Ulfen folk.⁠
1081989689:
Citadel Krane

Citadel Krane is the fortress-headquarters of the Hellknight Order of the Pyre, and can be found south of the Chelaxian city of Ostenso on Cape Erebus.⁠⁠

The seaside fortress is built into the rising shore cliffs around a natural harbor, overlooking both nearby land and sea. Citadel Krane is the only Hellknight citadel that hosts its own fleet of warships. Its fleet consists of nearly three-dozen black-sailed heavy ships shod in dark metal and crewed by lightly armored Hellknights.⁠

The citadel hosts the Godless Gallery, a museum of unholy artifacts and cultic writings that either defy destruction or hold the potential to be turned against their blasphemous creators. Priestly signifers protect the library, granting access only to the order's lictor, master of blades, and paravicar. The order's signifers also maintain the "undoctrination halls" within the fortress's bowels, where they liberate the heretics or savages from the bonds of their false beliefs.⁠

Mirazha

Years ago, the town of Mirazha in Katapesh was a waypoint for weary travelers, then an mysterious disaster struck the town. Mirazha was deserted and travelers found the bodies of the townsfolk in the oasis on the edge of town. The bodies were desiccated and withered, all the moisture seemingly drained. For a time, Mirazha stood abandoned. Eventually the desert sands covered over the town, the oasis dried up, and the town was forgotten. Recently, an evil has revived the memory of Mirazha and its doomed inhabitants. Travelers report seeing a little town on the edge of a sparkling oasis, but if someone enters the cursed town, the town and the new victim vanish from sight. Adventurers in the area have yet to spot the cursed town, but sometimes they find the mummified bodies of the victims, buried in the sand.⁠
1095473879:
Urglin

The predominantly orc⁠ city of Urglin (which means "Second Home" in the orc language) is the only population center of any sort in the Cinderlands region of Varisia's Storval Plateau.⁠
1097013119:
Mishkar

Unusually for a human community in Iobaria, Mishkar is not built from the scavenged remains of cyclopean ruins. Originally established in 809 AR as a guard post against threats from the Grenalf Plateau, it was abandoned by Iobaria around 4607 AR, only to be re-established by Varisian and Taldan settlers around 4659 AR.

The town has since become a largely self-sufficient city-state with a large agricultural and trade base. The people of Mishkar greatly value their independence and have remained unaffiliated with Iobaria's various factions, though they have forged an occasional alliance with centaur tribes against goblin hordes from the highlands.⁠

In 4719 AR, the town was damaged by a massive forest fire in the nearby Finadar Forest, but had largely recovered by 4720 AR.⁠
1098530079:
Lopul

Lopul is a large caravan city in the southern desert of Qadira.⁠
1147000259:
Morozny

The city of Morozny is the regional capital of the Irriseni province of Wintercrux.⁠

Aroden's Eye

Aroden's Eye is a rocky mountain with a circular hole 150 feet wide in the northeastern World's Edge Mountains of Taldor, east of the Thousand Relics Pass. It was named due to the similarity between its shape and Aroden's religious symbol, and was a frequent pilgrimage site for Arodenites, enough to support a small monastery consisting of twelve structures connected by rope bridges and narrow stairways.⁠⁠

After Aroden's death, the pilgrimages stopped, tithes no longer came, and the now-powerless clerics of Aroden abandoned the temple, except the old, bitter Leomaris Gurgin, who converted to the worship of Groetus. The desecrated temple has since then been inhabited by the Last Acolytes, a clan of harpies whom Gurgin converted to his new faith, and a handful of lunar nagas who serve as their astrologers. They sacrifice captives and recklessly summon murderous proteans, attracting redcaps and animate dreams in the process. Travellers report nightmares, with eerily similar descriptions of the mountain and a howling moon.⁠

Ivy Playhouse

The Ivy Playhouse is at the heart of Absalom, both physically and metaphysically, as the finest works from all of Golarion are presented daily in the theater, which changes with the seasons. The opera house is the base of operations for the Street Performers and Actors' Guild, led by Nomarch Alain Always, who acts in every performance, though not literally, as he relies on people who do cameos. He keeps a watchful eye out for new prodigies, and since the building houses an art gallery, there are always artists who come to showcase their talents. The Brotherhood of Abadar is trying to find some way to use the finances to stop the performances, which they consider too lascivious for Absalom. Although Alain has banned them from entering, they are outside harassing visitors, so they won't be stopped so easily.⁠
1166456389:
Safani

The settlement of Safani is a small town near the Crook River, in Osirion. Its leader is Efni Raan.

Safani is too far from major cities to receive the benefit of their protection against kholo raiders, so the town's residents came up with a unique defense strategy. The town is fully camouflaged: the buildings are built into the hills and covered in sod. Other vegetation has been carefully cultivated so it can cover more conspicuous aspects of the buildings, like doors and windows.⁠
1177559199:
Upslope House

Citadel Crest ward, in the Heights District, is the only ward in Korvosa having no inns by law. People requiring overnight stays, instead, have the choice from three bed and breakfast establishments, all of which are owned by nobles. In order of price, they are:

  • the Frisky Unicorn, the cheapest;
  • Upslope House; and
  • Tenna's, the most expensive.

In order of size, Tenna's is the smallest and Upslope House the largest.⁠

Upslope House has 10 rooms able to house 22 guests at a time. That this number is large for a mere bed and breakfast establishment, in an area where inns are forbidden, seems to be overlooked by the authorities.

City rumours hold that Upslope House hides a door to an area of the Vaults used by followers of an unnamed dark power. To add spice to the rumours, the involvement of dero is often thrown in.⁠
1184641509:
Macridi

The town of Macridi (pronounced ma-KRID-ee)⁠ is located in central Druma in the middle of the Palakar Forest, at the confluence of the Great Goldpan River and the Profit's Flow. It is primarily a logging town.⁠

Although just as affluent as the other population centers of the Kalistrocracy, Macridi's residents do not feel the need to display their wealth as openly. This gives the wooded town a somewhat less opulent feel.⁠

Jernashall was the preeminent city of the dwarven kingdom of Tar Khadurrm, and was located in the southern reaches of the Five Kings Range.

Grand Council Hall

The Grand Council Hall is a magnificent, large white marble structure where the city's most influential people meet to discuss the city's laws and administration. The 49 members of the Low Council meet monthly in a large hall with alcoves and stone thrones, where the acoustics provide good communication over long distances, though paradoxically, they also offer privacy for quiet conversations. Above these alcoves are the 13 seats of the High Council, which are in every respect superior to the others, and its members rarely appear in public except on the rare occasions when the entire body must vote on a motion, as they prefer to hold these debates in private rooms around the city.⁠

The general public can attend if they possess one of the tablets granted to the councillors, which in theory should be given to the city's military and heroes, but in practice end up in the hands of corrupt merchants and nobles who want to be close to those in power to see if they can plunder something like vultures. A series of underground passages connect to factories and scriptoriums where the council's bureaucracy is on full display, and the entire system is protected by a private guard at the service of the institution itself.⁠
1237940269:
Heaven's Ladder

Heaven's Ladder is a crematorium that offers an alternative to Godsmouth Ossuary, providing services at various prices to prevent bodies from ending up in the streets. Owned by Geph Hinsmen, it allows the families of the deceased to decide on funeral rites and priests before placing them in the crematorium.⁠
1244811339:
Azure Star

Azure Star is a popular restaurant deep in the Lower City district of Katapesh. From the outside it is a large gray tent covered in sky-blue stars. Inside the tent, private rooms are formed using silk partitions, and all rooms surround a large open common room with overlapping carpets covering the floor. Patrons lounge around small tables, on soft comfortable pillows. Musicians and singers entertain the guests who come to taste the exotic cuisine served there such as honeyed loci, curdled camel milk, pesh-sprinkled dhabba liver, pickled scorpion, grilled adder, thrice-poisoned oysters, and others. A bound air elemental creates a soft breeze to comfort Azure Star's guests.⁠
1249023699:
Ganagsau

Ganagsau is the largest set of Ghol-Gan ruins in the Cannibal Isles of the Shackles. It is also the location of their so-called deity, the Blood Queen. The Blood Queen is actually a powerful outsider of astounding power and evil who has transformed the kuru—people who were forced onto the islands—into primitive monsters.

The Blood Queen's current high priest is Bukrugsor. He serves in the Sanguine Cathedral as the intermediate between the kuru and their "goddess", making demands that include human sacrifices and other acts of repugnant devotion.⁠⁠
1256432439:
Castle of the Green Feather

The Castle of the Green Feather was the flying castle of the knights of the Order of the Green Feather. It could easily transport legions across long distances. The castle is thought to have survived Earthfall, but shortly thereafter the arcane magic keeping it aloft failed, and the fortress crash-landed on the Kodar Mountains near the modern-day northern border of Varisia. Some of the knights of the Order of the Green Feather were turned into graveknights and liches upon death, and they continue to guard their sacred fortress and serve the Peacock Spirit today.⁠⁠

Isseld

Isseld is a minor town on the Frozen Road in Irrisen's Feyfrost province where most people earn their living from the trade on the river. The settlement has recently become known as the center of the trade in "primitive wares", mostly carved fetishes and talismans crafted by the Kellid barbarians of the Realm of the Mammoth Lords.⁠

Dalun

Located in the south of the Irriseni province of Wintercrux on the Thundering River, Dalun is a small trade town that does business with the outside world.⁠

Though Dalun strongly encourages trade with the outside world, which is essential for Irrisen's survival, its diplomatic efforts are ruined because of the Irriseni raids launched from Redtooth and Saarbotten in the Verge to the west.⁠ Indeed, Dalun is derisively called 'Gentle Dalun' by the people of Saarbotten despite the fact that Dalun supplies most of Saarbotten's food.⁠

Dalun was responsible for supplying Redtooth and Saarbotten with grain and other foodstuffs. Nadya's bloodthirsty sister, Urgalaena, baroness of Saarbotten, often sabotaged Nadya's diplomatic attempts. Lady Nadya's chief steward, Betrona Harcatha, was actually a spy for her sister Urgalaena.⁠
1302071209:
Pastorling

Pastorling is a small Taldan hamlet that stands in both the literal and figurative shadow of the nearby fortress of Canalsguard. Pastorling is located at the intersection of three of the Lingian Prefecture's canals (alongside Canalsguard), and the reek of their stagnant waters has kept the hamlet free from significant aristocratic interference.

The Lingian Canals are notoriously dangerous, and at least some of this is due to one of Pastorling's residents: Lesah Voriovixis. To the town she is but a humble baker, but in reality she is the heart of a network of organised crime known as the Canal Syndicate. She cunningly encrypts her communications using a hidden cypher based on the braids and fillings of the pies she sends to certain underlings.⁠
1327617779:
Sticky Mermaid

The Sticky Mermaid has been a feature of Old Korvosa's northern dockside for nearly two centuries. One of many rough taverns across Korvosa that cater to sailors and their ilk, the Sticky Mermaid plays host to regular drunken brawls and, over the years, a sizeable number of deaths. The Sticky Mermaid goes through a regular cycle of brawls, being shut down by the Korvosan Guard, fines or bribes being paid, and then finally reopening. The already rough clientele is made only worse by Fishjack, a particularly potent and unpleasant local spirit that includes fermented fish eggs as one of its ingredients.⁠
1333073019:
Saresp Mountain

The cave-pocked Saresp Mountain, a peak in Mendev's far eastern reaches, was once the site of many ancient tombs as well as shelters for families seeking refuge from the harshest parts of winter. The caves hosted many Sarkorian refugees after the opening of the Worldwound, but all disappeared near the end of the Mendevian Crusades, their caves either sealed or apparently struck by grave robbers.⁠

Deep Sky

Under the elementalists' direction, it was constructed by four genies bound to obey their orders. However, the genies conspired to find a way to curse their masters, and succeeded in creating a curse that led to their masters' downfall.⁠

Castle Korvosa

Easily the most imposing structure in a city of monumental architecture, Castle Korvosa is the fortress-citadel home of the monarchs Korvosa. Tephu

Tephu, the City of the Reed People is a city in the Sphinx Basin region of Osirion named for the reed-covered marshlands where the rivers Crook and Asp join. Consequently, the city houses the largest academy of scribes in Osirion, who have preserved a massive catalogue of records from the time of its founding in -1605 AR by Djederet II, pharaoh and cleric of Nethys. Tephu's current leader is the preservationist governor: Haty-a of Tephu Deka An-Keret.⁠⁠

Duwwor

1392246769:
Boneglutton Pit

Ghouls were drawn to the area, consuming corpses and digging for more,⁠ and with the rubble they created altars to their foul deities. In the upper part of the pit, a cult of Urgathoa has formed, which throws corpses and live victims as sacrifices to the ghouls, lowering themselves on ropes to commune with them.⁠

Jezonna Oasis

Jezonna Oasis, or sometimes just Jezonna, is an oasis town located in the Meraz Desert of Qadira and is a rare source of both water and safety. It is headquarters to the Amellas al-Hekbah, an organization of desert giants granted imperial Kelesh citizenship as thanks for ensuring the safety of travellers crossing the Meraz Desert.⁠

Jezonna Oasis has several encampments of desert giant tribes spread between the oasis' three lakes, which are known as the Three Wisdoms. The most prominent of these tribes is led by Janar Malakra, who also leads the Amellas al-Hekbah's mercenary organization.⁠
1398782299:
Hall to the Broken Dream

The Hall to the Broken Dream is the name of both a location hidden in Nidal and the cult devoted to the velstrac demagogue Vevelor that dwells within.⁠

The hall itself seems to be constructed out of pure shadowstuff⁠ and the majority of its members are lampadarius velstracs who sheer off pieces of their own flesh to replace them with shadowstuff.⁠ Normally, lampadariuses serve the Midnight Lord Zon-Kuthon, but instead, those who dwell in the Hall to the Broken Dream worship Vevelor. Under the leadership of Skrialsiken, a velstrac who claims to be Vevelor's herald, the Hall to the Broken Dream has become a part of Nidalese society; every year, they send a delegation from the Hall to the capital city of Pangolais.⁠

Normally any other religion would not be tolerated within Nidal but the adherents of the Hall to the Broken Dream insist that their existence is simply the defying of predestination that limits the other followers of Zon-Kuthon. Indeed, many amongst the Umbral Court dislike the Hall and its followers of Vevelor, they are however tolerated since most laypeople of Nidal cannot discern the subtle differences of philosophy between Zon-Kuthon and Vevelor and the Umbral Court wants to avoid the appearance of factionalism within its ranks. The Hall to the Broken Dream secretly recruits from amongst the people of Nidal searching for atheists and Kuthites who possess both dissatisfaction with their lot in life and the iron will to ascend to something more than human. Within the Hall to the Broken Dream these mortal followers of Vevelor undergo horrific fleshwarping procedures in an attempt to ascend into velstracs.⁠

Xiwu

The fortress city of Xiwu, one of the most populated settlements of Tian Xia—or indeed, on Golarion—is the capital of militaristic Lingshen. The city appears to be a military installation unlike anything else in the world.⁠
1408772419:
Ndele Gap

The Ndele Gap is a high-altitude mountain pass in western Nex between the Barrier Wall to the north and the Shattered Range to the south.⁠

It is the most obvious and frequently travelled eastern route into the Mwangi Expanse, and Taldor's ill-fated Sixth Army of Exploration marched through the Gap on its way to disaster in the jungle.⁠

The thin air and cold temperatures make travel difficult, and travellers are occasionally attacked by bandits and kholo.⁠
1410265109:
Aromas and Aphrodisiacs

Aromas and Aphrodisiacs is a pavilion of brightly colored tents connected to each other, with a scent that attracts anyone who approaches.⁠ The herbalist Chiaong runs the establishment with his slaves, offering herbs that can be inhaled, drunk, or applied to the skin to create a relaxing sensation in the user.⁠
1417113559:
Temple of Nethys

The Temple of Nethys in Katapesh is an enormous pyramid with a multicolored flame that burns without any fuel. Inside, the vast space features walls decorated with the tenents of Nethys, while guards in masks and half-white, half-black robes watch to prevent thieves from entering.⁠ One of the rooms contains a library of arcane knowledge that the priests share among themselves to further their research into magical creations or their principles and their head priest Bale Politiz watches over these experiments.⁠
1422011419:
Scar of the Spider

The Scar of the Spider is a small, fungi-encrusted vale in the southwestern Felldales of Numeria, just north of the West Sellen River. Generally avoided by everyone, this valley of gray stone spears is said to be the home of a steel arachnid that strikes terror into even the stoutest warriors. Other legends tell of a glass coffin located somewhere in the vale, wherein writhes a dancing and whistling enigma.⁠
1422367449:
Orkatto's Feathers and Fur

Orkatto's Feathers and Fur caters to those nouveau riche of Korvosa who have a taste for exotic pets. The unique store is located in the newer South Shore district of the Varisian city. The store is a strange wonderland of exotic animals, from caged songbirds to gem-hued snakes, all the way up to dream spiders which are valued by Orkatto's more shady clientele for their venom, which can be refined into a powerful drug called shiver. The store's owner, Orkatto, served as a well-respected master of the hunt to a powerful lord in the nearby city of Magnimar, before finally saving enough money to open his own namesake store.⁠

Citadel Volshyenek

Citadel Volshyenek is the headquarters of the Korvosan Guard. It can be found at the end of a short spit of land sticking out from the Midland District into the Jeggare River.⁠⁠
1480814809:
Kalexcourt

Kalexcourt, the Fortress of Monoliths, or the Vault of the Witch-Priests, stands at the very north-westernmost point of Ustalav, in the county of Vieland, among the lower slopes of the Tusk Mountains.⁠ It is an ancient burial mound of the Kellid peoples dating from before the founding of Ustalav.⁠
1485086109:
Golemworks

The Golemworks is one of the most iconic industries in Magnimar. As its name implies, it produces golems.⁠⁠

Raliscrad

Westgate Bathhouse

The Westgate Bathhouse is one of the most popular establishments of its kind in the city, receiving visitors day and night who come to enjoy its spacious pools. The marble structure gives it a cathedral-like feel due to its size, and it offers massage services, a market, and private pools for couples or those plotting plans and deals.⁠
1525287289:
Citadel Vraid

Citadel Vraid is the fortress-headquarters of the Hellknight Order of the Nail, indeed it is sometimes referenced as the Fortress of the Nail.⁠ It was constructed by the city of Korvosa in an effort to successfully entice the Order to move to Varisia. It is located about 50 miles southwest of Korvosa on a narrow plateau named after one of Korvosa's founders, Montlarion Jeggare, and is on the edge of the southern Mindspin Mountains.⁠
1526303919:
Bailey's Perch

Bailey's Perch is a small village on the shore of Lake Encarthan in Druma, far enough north not to be on the Gulf of Accord. It's a quiet, simple fishing community that recently caught an undead fish, which is the talk of the town.⁠
1547033589:
Warden's Shack

Warden's Shack is located at the end of the New Fish Trail in Brinestump Marsh and is the residence of Walthus Proudstump. Since the ranger dislikes socializing, he spends his afternoons alone fishing or selling the furs he hunts to those who venture along the path to his home.⁠

1568981139:
Sable Barrow

Sable Barrow is a hill that overlooks the Numerian city of Chesed.⁠⁠ The Pathfinder Gojan the Sharp observed a golden statue appear on the Barrow the night before a seemingly inevitable slave revolt. The statue hefted a mighty hammer and seemed to be threatening the city with it, and carried the mark of the god Abadar on his chest armor. Gojan believed that the statue's presence prevented the slave revolt, and it disappeared four days later. Most agree that the golden statue was actually the Lawgiver, the herald of Abadar.⁠

Lawgiver's appearance instead inspired the slaves to join with the city's defenders in order to repel an unprecedented, and since unequaled, assault upon the city by barbarians. After the city's successful defense against the raid, Chesed abolished its slave trade, emancipated its slaves, and decreed that any slave brought into the city would be declared free within an hour of arrival if not registered with the city's government.⁠
1573732869:
Mephit Spring

Mephit Spring is a valley in the Footprints of Rovagug mountains of western Osirion that is the locus of several powerful elemental forces. Located between the Kho-Rarne Pass and Tar Kuata, the springs were once the home of many scamps who communed peacefully with one another. As of 4714 AR, the mood darkened, as a demon had taken over the area.⁠⁠
1579157589:
Fort Machema

Fort Machema is an abandoned fort a few days' journey from Tamran along the shore of Lake Encarthan. The fort is in a well-protected area overlooking the lake, but there are no soldiers to maintain it.⁠
1596091669:
Palace of Birdsong

The Palace of Birdsong is one of the traditional estates of Taldor's current ruling family, House Stavian. It is located at the heart of the Stavian Barony in Meratt County of Taldor's Tandak Prefecture, near Lotheedar.⁠
1620026659:
Sunken Queen

The Sunken Queen, once known as the Shining Queen,⁠ is a partially submerged Thassilonian pyramid built over 10,000 years ago by the Runelord Sorshen⁠ in what was then the nation of Eurythnia.⁠ It is located in southern Varisia in an enormous swampland known as the Mushfens, approximately 160 miles west of the city of Korvosa.⁠⁠
1631517119:
Golquila

The walled city of Golquila is one of the numerous prosperous ports that rim the Betul Sea in the Western Ghats region of the Impossible Kingdoms of Vudra. Its defences are enhanced by being built into the mountains. Further protection for the city is provided by two huge gorillas and their keepers who stay near the city. Golquila is located at one end of the Seabound Road, the completion of which heralded a new era of prosperity for the once-desolate region of the Western Ghats.⁠
1632382099:
Thap Samut

Thap Samut (pronounced: Tahp sahm-oot⁠) is the northernmost city of the sorcerous nation of Tang Mai, located in the far north-east of the country. Thap Samut also serves as Tang Mai's largest port, where fortunes can be rapidly made and easily lost.⁠
1641993119:
Tarnished Temple

The Tarnished Temple is a ruined structure on an islet that rose up alongside Xin in 4712 AR. At the top of the temple, a group of adventurers were able to summon the spirit of Zutha using part of the Gluttonous Tome to destroy him, and since then, fragments of his necromantic energy have caused unusual effects in the upper levels. Below, the temple has been occupied by various aquatic creatures who worship powerful sea beings, which they incorrectly assume the temple's decayed statues represent.⁠
1642201629:
Ayin Lun

Ayin Lun is a long-lost ruined city in northern Mendev that had been overridden by undead in generations past. Survivors of the city erased all records of the city after its destruction, and its suspected site was revealed only after the death of Gorum in 4724 AR.

Possibly during the Godsrain that ensued, nine stony spires erupted across Mendev, each containing a gap at several hundred feet of elevation that purportedly lead to strange lands of hostile beings. These towers became known among Mendevians as Godsfall towers.

As of 4725 AR, the towers' purpose and origins are unknown, and Mendevian Chancellor Irahai had officially prohibited climbing the towers and posted guards at each. The towers nonetheless remained scaled by young native Mendevians who consider them to be rites of passage, and many have successfully returned from their attempts.⁠
1667072579:
El-Amara

The ruins of el-Amara are in western Osirion, close to the border with Thuvia. The ruins lie close to where the Junira River and the Scarab River meet.⁠

On the other side of the Junira, in nearby Thuvia, are the Ruins of Akhenaten.⁠

El-Amara was once the provincial capital of Thuvia, when Thuvia was still part of the Ancient Osirion. It was abandoned and fell to ruin when pharaohs started to ignore their distant vassal state. It was in el-Amara that High Theurgist Fentet-Pesu, the last Osirian governor of Thuvia, was assassinated in -841 AR. Since its fall, few had visited the half-buried spires and crumbling bell towers of el-Amara, until a few centuries ago when disciples of Ahriman took to the ruins to establish a base near Osirion. As of 4712 AR, el-Amara was populated by sepid divs led by general Karesh-Ekhial and hordes of ghul and edimmu thralls.⁠
1684459049:
Utterhome

Utterhome is the base of operations for the Sleepless Suns, the guard of Absalom's Foreign Quarter. The structure was a manor in the Osirian style, complete with Jadwiga ice statues, glass panels imported from New Thassilon, Tian Xia-style pools, and Vudrani area gardens, the fortress reflects the district's diversity.⁠ The very name Utterhome represents the many ways in which languages ​​refer to the concept of home, and all people are welcome regardless of their cultural background. The guard's name also has a similar concept, indicating that the sun never sets for them, as their members come from all over the world. Therefore, when it is night in Absalom, it is day in Tian Xia, and its members embody that devotion to citizen protection.⁠
1686919939:
Pho Yim

Pho Yim, sometimes written Mount Pho-Yim, is an enormous volcano located in the south of Tang Mai that looms over the nation's capital of Surat Prakan and is a part of the vast Kullan Dei mountain range. While Pho Yim is currently not active, it does smoke ominously⁠ and it is rumoured that its molten fury is only held at bay by the harmony of the five sorcerous rulers of Tang Mai.⁠ Nevertheless, During the Age of Ascendancy, the volcano did erupt explosively destroying much of Tang Mai in 7099 IC and, some say, in consequence of the invasion of the country by Lung Wa some years previously.⁠

The local hero Ankilhi used the fires of Pho Yim to forge a tetsubo out of the remains of the graveknight Pnao Kilnak.⁠
1692509499:
Old Detmer

Old Detmer is the nickname given by the locals to the underwater ruins of the city of an ancient civilization. Standing stones and antimagic wards scattered around the area make it difficult to explore fully.⁠
1700545149:
Jalunth

Jalunth is a village of Ekujae in the central Mwangi Jungle region of the Mwangi Expanse approximately 100 miles southeast of Nantambu.⁠ Due to years of difficult experience with outsiders, the residents rarely share even the name of their village with non-Ekujae.⁠ Finding Jalunth in the dense jungle terrain is difficult without appropriate local guides or skilled trackers.⁠
1711596599:
Skull's Crossing

Skull's Crossing is the name of the massive arched dam that holds back the waters of the Storval Deep, releasing a steady stream into the Skull River.⁠ Located in central Varisia it is an ancient ruin from the Thassilonian era over 10,000 years ago.⁠⁠⁠
1724086379:
Furrow & Vine

Furrow & Vine is a shop that has been selling vegetables and fruit for almost a century, run by Parnham Nollins. Nobody in the district considers him an enemy and the shop is free from suspicion except for rumors that revolutionaries meet inside to discuss their plans.⁠
1727665769:
Sand Dragon Inn

The Sand Dragon Inn sits along the southern side of the Golden Oasis. Travelers often stop here before exploring the city of Katapesh further on. A serpentine dragon perches above the main entrance of the inn.⁠
1731011459:
Voinum Estate

The Voinum Estate is located about three miles outside of the village of Voinaris, at the heart of the Voinum Barony in Taldor's Tandak Prefecture. It serves as the ancestral seat of the vaunted House Voinum.

The estate features one of the most extensive wine cellars in northern Taldor, including centuries-old bottles, and the rest of the estate houses secret rooms containing rare recipes and yeast for winemaking drawn from across Avistan.⁠
1731704489:
Stone of the Seers

Magnimar's most respectable school of arcane instruction, the Stone of the Seers, stands next to the Seerspring Gardens and its legendary spring.⁠
1735362289:
Undervale

Undervale is a way station in the Umbral Basin that also serves as a safe haven for the Bellflower Network. The area is teeming with predators and potential trouble, but it also offers an opportunity for those seeking to escape Cheliax or Nidal. Constructs and illusions protect the station, and part of it is built underground. Its residents are mostly halflings whose cheerful and welcoming nature is a warm welcome.⁠⁠

The leader of Undervale is undoubtedly Landry Tethertine, who maintains the constructs and seeks new members to join the station.⁠
1749355269:
Clenchjaw's

Clenchjaw's, named for its owner Rinston "Clenchjaw" Jom, was once a much quieter tavern than it is now. Sitting in the Yolubilis Harbor district of Kintargo meant that, when the nearby Thrashing Badger burned down during the Night of Ashes, Clenchjaw's gained an influx of rowdy dockworkers and wannabe revolutionaries that has disrupted the once quieter bar.⁠ Now brawls and intrigue have become a regular part of the bar's life.⁠

Little known to either Clenchjaw's owner or its patrons is that much of this trouble is due to a new resident, a mischievous faerie dragon intent on causing trouble.⁠
1756196529:
Moak Harbor

Moak Harbor was a port city on Shark Island in the Shackles that was home to more than 8,000 people at its peak more than 200 years ago, but today is only rotting ruins.⁠
1759942849:
F & M's Exotic Meats

F & M's Exotic Meats, located in the Low Eastwind district, is a unique butcher's shop in the pirate capital of Port Peril.

F & M's Exotic Meats is run by the odd pairing of Mizrah, an aiuvarin cleric of the goddess of invention Brigh, and Festerscale, a kobold. With their unique magical storerooms that keep the meat cool, they can provide fresh meat to the people of Port Peril despite the tropical heat. They provide meat for a range of customers, from expensive prime beef and outrageous exotic meats to basic sausages.

Fewer people know that F & M's Exotic Meats also disposes of unwanted corpses, typically by surreptitiously incorporating them into one of their other clients' meals.⁠
1760545239:
Claes

The Andoren fishing village of Claes is located on the Inner Sea coast, just over 50 miles south of the Andoshen River delta. A humble town, the inhabitants make their living from the ample harvest of the sea, supplementing it with some subsistence farming. When pirates or slavers attack, the people of Claes retreat to an ancient, underground Azlanti fortress known as the Claes Redoubt; the ruin is known to be quite deep.⁠⁠

General Reginald Cormoth, commander of Andoran's Eagle Knights, was born in Claes.⁠
