Lipror

Lipror sits on stilts over the Matra River delta where it meets the Embaral Ocean. Known as "The City of Lotuses", Lipror is one of many prosperous cities that make up the fertile region of Wide Water.⁠ Lipror is an active trade partner with the upstream city of Radripal, whose people share a common faith in Matravash and engage in annual pilgrimages to each others' holy sites.⁠
1774350479:
Segada

Segada is a city of Mahwek Arcadians that serves as a gateway to Degasi and other reaches of Arcadia's interior. Its economic importance, already significant as a hub for Arcadian commerce, has grown from recent trade with Avistan.⁠
1775570259:
Gitna

Gitna is an iruxi settlement that has existed here since before Geb and Nex began their conflict.⁠
1779116489:
Shoreline Drinkhall

Shoreline Drinkhall is the most popular tavern in the East Shore district of Korvosa. Its main clientele are off-duty Korvosan Guard members who come through three times a day when the shift changes and longshoremen who visit every evening. Many other East Shore residents also stop by for drinks and, due to Shoreline Drinkhall's close proximity to the Thief Camp area, it also attracts many Shoanti and Varisians. Bar brawls occur fairly regularly but are not quite as dangerous as those at some of the city's other establishments like, for example, the Sticky Mermaid. The Shoreline Drinkhall has a reputation for fair prices, stiff drinks, and meals that are closer to military rations than to civilian food. The establishment is owned by House Endrin.⁠ For those requiring more privacy, private areas are available in the tavern.⁠
1779416929:
Kassen

Kassen is a small town on the Tourondel River in the Fangwood of Nirmathas. It is a relatively close-knit settlement with origins that stretch back to the year 4522 AR, when the town's founder, Ekat Kassen, grew tired of life as an adventurer and retired there.⁠
1782376019:
Five-Fire Pavilions

The Five-Fire Pavilions is a burnt-out structure with exposed blackened metal beams that can be considered Absalom's goblin embassy, ​​led by the explorer Skirma Toadlicker, who seeks to show that goblins are ready to join the "civilized" world.⁠

Many goblins, hobgoblins, and others considered monsters have attended the pavilion's exhibitions, art displays, and fireworks, trading amongst themselves. However, not all cultural exchanges go smoothly, especially when a neighbor walks their dog, which some goblins interpret as a meat offering. There are also rivalries between tribes and differences between those who seek a more savage life, insulting hobgoblins who ride horses, and the more civilized, who call their less educated kin deformed. Even so, Skirma hopes that things will be better in the future and that this is a step forward.⁠
1782756229:
Deepgate

Deepgate is a huge stone and iron fortress located deep in the Kodar Mountains of the Hold of Belkzen, to the east of the source of the Kazaron River.⁠
1788932959:
Morast

Morast is a small village in the Dippelmere Swamp approximately eight miles east of the city of Lepidstadt in Ustalav.⁠
1795568459:
Shinju-no-Ie

Shinju-no-Ie was the residence of the pearl merchant Yugureda Shosaito, having been a beautiful seaside villa in the past, but now it appears more abandoned than anything else. The vibrant colors of the roof and walls have faded, and the iron gates are rusted and creak when someone opens them, indicating that the rest of the estate is in a similar condition.⁠
1800141279:
Merev

Merev is a city on Yanimere Island, off the western coast of Qadira across from the Ketz Desert.⁠
1803101729:
Dalaston

Dalaston is a large town on the southwestern edge of Taldor's World's Edge Mountains.⁠ Although members of all the major races reside in the town, dwarves are the second-largest group after humans. The three major employers are the local iron mine (owned by the Dalassenos family), the Morian Foundry, and the Irini brewery.⁠

In 4709 AR, the red dragon Horranath attacked Dalaston.⁠

In 4725 AR, the Godsrain awakened a dragon that devastated the village, and only a few inhabitants have not left the area.⁠
1807859319:
Falling Runewheel

The Falling Runewheel is one of the cyclopean monuments of ancient Thassilon, built with the labor of enslaved rune and stone giants.⁠ It is located off the western coast of modern Varisia, which was the Thassilonian nation of Bakrakhan.⁠
1822277339:
Seaward Fort

The Seaward Fort is built on one of the two small islands of Corentyn's harbor to the south of the city, known as the Navy Yard district. It serves as the head of naval command for the Chelaxian Navy.⁠

The Seaward Fort is one of the nine famous forts of Corentyn, the City of Nine Forts, according to the classical listing.⁠
1822447739:
Raketooth

Raketooth is the second-largest port on Shark Island in the Shackles. It is a dreary settlement specializing in pilfered luxury wares that are usually sold on Motaku Isle or to the few non-slaver merchants who come to Shark Island. Raketooth rarely has difficulties with sedacthies who plague the island. The pirate lords of Raketooth, Mauril Breakwater and "Baron" Venigo Palpathe, maintain the relative peace of the town by providing tribute to the nearby sedacthy tribes.⁠
1825480859:
Gardens of Delight

The Gardens of Delight, or Garden of Delights, are a gigantic tiered group of gardens located in the Holoma province of Juttar. The gardens are presided over by Juttar's Grand Omwa Holo Enyana's palace, and host not only beautiful plants but also a large menagerie of unusual and magical animals. The wildlife here is entirely tame, and celestial hybrids of dinosaurs native to Holomog display particularly unusual and eye-catching characteristics.⁠
1835423529:
Battle of Grasyhot

The site of the Battle of Grasyhot can be found northeast of the Numerian capital of Starfall, just south of the Egelsee River near the border with Mendev. In it, the forces of the Kellid Queen Boliga Bharsolm fought with the 30 tribes of the hill giant chief Urgo Axbiter. The battle began in 1288 AR and continued on and off for three years, with both sides experiencing advances and retreats. When Axbiter was killed, his followers erected a huge earthen mound over his grave near the battlefield, so that he might continue to inspire them in death. The climactic confrontation of the battle ended in victory for the Kellid tribes. Queen Bharsolm met her death during it, and was interred in a similar earthen tomb at the battle site, so that she might eternally delight in the hill giants' defeat. Both burial mounds still stand today, a lasting tribute to heroism and determination.⁠⁠
1838136209:
Tower of Slant Shadows

Located in the southwestern plains of Nidal, the Tower of Slant Shadows is a rugged iron edifice that juts diagonally from the umber grassland. It is believed that it sinks several times its own height into the earth beneath it. A mystery to most, the tower is in fact one of the almost-forgotten Star Towers, constructed untold millennia ago by Zon-Kuthon (then Dou-Bral) as part of the process necessary to confine Rovagug within Golarion.⁠⁠
1842192589:
Skjoldmur

Skjoldmur is a small whaling town in the south of the island of Aegos, the larger island comprising Broken Bay in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings.⁠⁠
1846740159:
Vira Salisfer

Vira Salisfer is the social hub of Islatra, Rego Laina, serving as the center of power for Westcrown's small but surprisingly influential House Salisfer. The black walls are protected by barbicans, giving the place the impression of a keep.⁠
1847518669:
Saruhk

Saruhk is a small religious community and temple complex located in the northwestern jungles of the Mwangi Expanse. It is protected from the outside world by Anwigasi, the divine herald of the empyreal lord Winlas.⁠
1864870289:
Saringallow

The Isgeri town of Saringallow is located on the Conerica River, south of the capital of Elidir.⁠
1881744229:
Band of the Palm Headquarters

The Band of the Palm Headquarters is where the Bloody Barbers criminal gang gathers for their operations throughout the city. Under the guise of the Band of the Palm, a union of chimney sweeps, garbage collectors, and cleaners operate out of this series of buildings that include offices, sleeping quarters, bankrupt businesses, and warehouses, all connected by ropes and bridges that make it difficult to distinguish one building from another. Legitimate members live in the area closest to the entrance, while below, the Barbers operate in a series of catacombs, sewers, and caverns guarded by the Ghostguides, a group of albino chokers who show the way to the base where the leaders reside—an impenetrable fortress. In a room hidden even from the guides, Dr. Bensi Skule experimented on a troll prisoner who would become the gang's leader.⁠
1898468089:
Souston

Souston is a small Andoren fishing village on the Inner Sea, approximately 240 miles due east of the capital of Almas. The town consists of small, brightly colored shacks that cling to the gently sloping coast.⁠⁠
1902081249:
Northman's Woodworks Galleria

Northman's Woodworks Galleria is a shop run by the busy Hans the Northman, one of the best, if not the best, woodworker in all of Absalom. Orders can be placed at the entrance, or you can pay a fee to walk around the workshop, as there is also a gallery of great interest to those with a passion for woodworking.⁠
1910400239:
College of Mysteries


The College of Mysteries (formerly known as the House of Secrets) is the oldest school of magic in Absalom and is located in the Petal District. The college has a superb reputation in the city and is favored by a number of organisations, such the Javelin Gallery, whom they aid by enchanting weapons.⁠
1916832809:
Sicnavier's Lair

Sicnavier's Lair is a dark chasm located in the Hungry Mountains in eastern Virlych, a grim mountain range in southern Ustalav.⁠

A place haunted by the spirits of evil dragons, Sicnavier's Lair is always ruled by a sole umbral dragon who had succeeded the previous draconic master. The spoils of this rivalry is an enormous accumulation of wealth, lore, and slaves, more than enough to convince the successor to ignore ghostly whispers, even as the growing number of restless ghosts attempt to drive them insane.⁠

Whichever dragon controls the lair names themselves 'Sicnavier', a title that has passed to no fewer than six dragons over the centuries. Attempts by outsiders to slay the dragon usually fail, but on those rare occasions when an attempt succeeds, a new, younger dragon takes on the mantle for him or herself.

The deepest pits of Sicnavier's Lair connects to the Darklands, although the dragon master and the creatures below have limited interaction with one another.⁠

As of 4711 AR the ruler was Sicnavier VI, a very old umbral dragon who is said to have been driven to near madness from the tormenting whispers of its slain kin. Other inhabitants, such as Dark folk, nightwings, and tenebrous worms, also inhabit the lair and are most frequently slaves or pets of their draconic overlord.⁠
1918313149:
Thornkeep

The small town of Thornkeep is located within the Echo Wood of the northwestern River Kingdoms, about 10 miles east of the West Sellen River and 100 miles northwest of Daggermark at the junction of the Mosswater, Dagger, and Forest roads. Its reputation as a rowdy and dangerous settlement draws unscrupulous adventurers, bandits, and entrepreneurs for many types of illicit trade.⁠⁠ The large number of nearby ruins and monsters attracts many adventurers looking to start making a name for themselves.⁠ This includes those interested in the nearby Emerald Spire.⁠

Thornkeep has a wizard's guild called the Goldenfire Order.⁠
1931700389:
Saddlebark Ranch

Saddlebark Ranch is a breeder and trainer of faerie mounts and Taldan corgis located in the foothills of the Kortos Mounts on the Isle of Kortos. Its proprietor is Timblethorn Baublebrand, who launched the ranch after recognizing that riding dogs were more surefooted than axebeaks or camels in the Mounts.

Once an innovator, Saddlebark was as of 4720 AR merely one of a dozen such ranches in the region, and the Aspis Consortium had been bullying ranchers and acquiring property for a cut of the business.⁠
1943479719:
Helkgen

Helkgen is a small town on the shores of Glacier Lake in the Irriseni province of Bleakmarch.⁠

The Ulfen residents of Helkgen are struggling to support the merchant ships hugging the shores of Glacier Lake as Jadwiga overlords demand, but also to collect sufficient tribute throughout the year to give to the unforgiving scrags of Scrag Deep.⁠

As of 4713 AR, Helkgen's mayor was Valka Dagsdottir, who earned the ire of townsfolk while working hard to keep them safe from the scrags.⁠

Tomb of the Necrophage

The Tomb of the Necrophage is the mausoleum of a minor aristocrat from Yamasa named Mifutu, but after the country's destruction by the Eye of Abendego, a group of cannibalistic cultists moved into the area and began devouring corpses, setting traps throughout. Unholy symbols of Urgathoa, Rovagug, and Zura fill the chambers, and undead and elementals fight amongst themselves for control. The upper levels are completely flooded, and a small rift between planes is what has allowed elementals to enter the complex, while the rest of the complex is protected by wards and constructs that activate when anyone disturbs the tombs.⁠

Mount Kazunan

Mount Kazunan is a volcano in central Minkai along the Kyojin Mountains west of the Ningyo Gulf. It is one of the Three Fires, along with Mount Kumijinja in the Kamifushi Mountains and Mount Yogan in the southern Kyojin Mountains.⁠
1966173239:
Icebow Bridge

The village of Icebrow Bridge is a darkly scenic and quaint little village that sits in the centre of the shadowy nation of Nidal. Icebrow Bridge would be an unremarkable little village were it not for the Library Without Light, a vast collection of ancient, pre-Earthfall Azlanti and Thassilonian texts that were brought by fleeing survivors of this ancient apocalypse to Nidal. The ancient scrolls and books cover a wide variety of often obscure topics but have zero cohesion as a collection, as they were whatever texts their long-dead owners valued enough to take with them when fleeing their homes. The head librarian Hale Craggox controls access to the Library Without Light. Due to the prestige of the library, Icebrow Bridge is considered quite a desirable posting for agents of the Umbral Court.⁠
1970844379:
Chitterhome

Chitterhome is the largest ratfolk settlement in Numeria and serves as a de facto capital to the ysoki ethnicity of Numerian Tinkerers.⁠ It is located in the Sellen Hills region, about 50 miles east of Scrapwall. The settlement itself is a square mile in size and consists of natural caverns that have been further excavated.⁠

Chitterhome contains three, and possibly more, carefully guarded entrances to Nar-Voth.⁠

Outsiders are not allowed in Chitterhome, but its residents trade throughout eastern Numeria, particularly Chesed, Hajoth Hakados, and along the Sellen River.⁠
1979327759:
Severed Spiral

The Severed Spiral is a circle of 43 standing stones surrounding seven dolmens located deep within the Estrovian Forest of Mendev. The western half of the circle's stones are made of dark, rough-hewn basalt and other dark-colored stones, while the eastern stones are made of white, smooth dolomite.⁠⁠

The circle is the only permanent holy site of the Children of Balance, an organization of religious two-headed trolls led by Romrix who worship deities that most closely embody the duality and dichotomy of their lives—especially Pharasma, Nethys,⁠⁠ and Gozreh.⁠
1991946499:
Market District

The Market District of Urgir, the de facto capital of the Hold of Belkzen, is located in the western side of the city's first tier just inside the western gate. It is the center of trade in Urgir and home to most of its non-orc residents, the majority of whom were invited by the late overlord Grask Uldeth's dromaar diplomats. Most of the market's permanent merchants were drawn out of desperation or because they traded in illegal goods, such as drugs, poisons, or slaves.⁠
1999733949:
Pediment Building

The Pediment Building contains the Office of the Lord-Mayor, plus Magnimar's primary court and the Halls of Virtue, as well as its only prison.⁠ The latter is located beneath the building: a prison known to all Magnimar as "The Hells". The Pediment Building is located atop the wealthy Summit region in the Capital District near the Usher's Hall. The building itself is large and intimidating, its vast exterior topped with imposing architecture and scowling gargoyles. Its inhabitants are scarcely less intimidating: the stern faced judges of Magnimar's Justice Court.⁠

Fenworth Gameporium

Fenworth Gameporium is a card and deck factory that creates, locates, and distributes various games throughout the city, being popular among the casinos and nobles of Absalom who are always looking for new forms of entertainment.⁠

City of Bleeding Stones

The City of Bleeding Stones is the largest set of Ghol-Gan ruins on the island of Devil's Arches in the Shackles. It is nestled in a cove beside the island's vast, hilly rainforests. Many major expeditions have been sent to the City of Bleeding Stone, but each has ended in disaster, even in the expedition's group complete disappearance. The few survivors claim that some primordial evil plagues the ruins. The Pathfinder Society has expressed interest in exploring the city.⁠
2016995249:
Shoreline

Shoreline is a small town located just outside the never-breached walls of Absalom, directly west of the district called the Puddles⁠⁠ and the Sally Port.⁠
2019175379:
Fort Nunder

Fort Nunder is the Chernasardo Rangers' stronghold closest to the Nesmian Plains of Nirmathas. It sits against the west side of a steep hill called Nunder Scarp. Decades ago, the Rangers constructed a vault beneath the hill to secure specialized weapons and equipment. The two best trapsmiths among the Rangers, Dargrit Foehewer and Ekaterin Fletcher, built two separate, trapped passages leading to the vault. Fort Nunder is more of a storehouse than a fortress. A handful of barracks are available, but the bulk of the fort is dedicated to storage space.⁠⁠⁠

2042488919:
Golden Oasis

The last remaining oasis that once gave the city of Katapesh its ancient name of the Golden City, the Golden Oasis is still a bastion of lush beauty. Once Katapesh had several such oases but after the Year of Scouring Winds the Golden Oasis was the only one that remained. It is feed by the River Scorpius and is surrounded by date palms and an area of quiet inns, homes and small shops, Golden Oasis is one of the first areas a lot of traders (those who enter via the Dawn Gate) see. Legend says that those who sit by the fish-filled central pool are sometimes granted visions of divine inspiration as a result many pilgrims can be found sat beneath the palms that surround the central oasis meditating. Some pilgrims leave satisfied, some just leave, others in their desperation resort to eating local spirit moss. This strange plant tastes disgusting but allows those who eat it to commune with the spirits of the dead and may be responsible for the reputation of the Golden Oasis.⁠
2046578759:
Osibu

The streets of the southeastern city of Osibu⁠ are literally paved with gold. Located in the Screaming Jungle within the greater Mwangi Expanse, the city is protected by a ring of statues called the Circle of Twice-Honored Women, which somehow reduces the cacophony of noise from the jungle and also keeps out the jungle's carnivorous plant life. Osibu is incredibly well hidden, with many maps not even acknowledging its existence, or misleading readers to another city or ruin within the Mwangi Expanse. Finding the city is an ordeal that involves many trials with the dangerous flora and fauna along the way.⁠

The city is a democracy, and life is a veritable utopia for its inhabitants. There are plentiful supplies of fruit and water, and the city's wise-women are able to mix rare herbs to produce an ointment which greatly extends life and staves off diseases.

Osibu is home to possibly Golarion's oldest living creature, the hunched arboreal regent Dimari-Diji, Final Tree of the Elder World. The ancient arboreal regent's first memory is the impact of Earthfall nearly ten thousand years ago. Dimari-Diji guards the Nemesis Well, a way between worlds.⁠

2083001879:
Asuulek's Mouth

Asuulek's Mouth (sometimes spelt Asulek's Mouth) is the most active of Osirion's two volcanoes and the lair of the ancient red wyrm Asuulek, for which it is named.⁠ At its summit is a large magma lake, and the volcano frequently spews out toxic gases, ash, and lava bombs onto the nearby area.⁠ Small communities work the fertile soil around the base of Asuulek's Mouth, however, they do so with a watchful eye, keeping watch for both eruptions and dragons.⁠

Some locations on Golarion are infused with elemental power and Asuulek's Mouth is one such location. Occasionally, a person living near Asuulek's Mouth will be touched by the fiery elemental energies of the volcano and gain the extraordinary ability to rapidly heal when covered in the ashes of destructive fire.⁠
2089563869:
Berus

Berus is a very prosperous settlement along the northern border of the Ustalavic county of Ardeal on the banks of the River of Scales.⁠⁠⁠
2093245359:
Escadar

Escadar is a city on the Isle of Erran off the north coast of the Isle of Kortos. It houses a city-sized military outpost, acting as one of Absalom's primary bases of naval operations.⁠⁠
2109148259:
Karcau

The city of Karcau (pronounced KAHR-cow)⁠ is the only major population center in the land of Sinaria in Ustalav. It is renowned as a shining light of civilisation in a region of dark, dreary wilderness. The city is most famous for the Karcau Opera and has a reputation as a place that both produces musical genius and fosters it, it is this reputation that has lead to Karcau's nickname of the Village of Voices. Karcau is nestled on the banks of Lake Prophyria and its waters cut their way through the city, criss-crossing it in various canals. These canals mirror the situation below the city as Karcau was built atop an underground lake and its foundations are shot through with underwater tunnels creating a mostly submerged labyrinth.⁠⁠
2109575089:
Chotilema's Boudoir

Chotilema's Boudoir is an underground and underwater cavern in the western foothills of the mountains of Zi Ha in Wanshou. Once the lair of the bog witch Chotilema, it is filled with all manner of undead abominations, molds, and slimes that have never seen the light of day.⁠
2109928909:
Miratanza

Miratanza, also known as the Floating Market, is located in the Rego Laina in Westcrown. It is the only area open to transactions and commerce on Westcrown Island or the Parego Regicona. It allows servants for the inhabitants of Regicona to shop for goods without visiting the mainland. Vendors can rent space or simply sell from ships tied up at the market.⁠⁠
2111275789:
Watercleft

The Watercleft is a cliff on the border between the Petal District and Eastgate, where a spring is moved by aqueducts, creating a beautiful view. There is much social activity in the area as people come to collect water from the spring. The distribution of water through private tunnels is seen as a disgrace by the residents of Green Ridge, which was once a separate district from Eastgate with its own council. After being absorbed, the people of Green Ridge lamented the loss of the values ​​that made the Watercleft so appealing.⁠
2112387449:
Hillview Station

Hillview Station is the Lotus Guard's base of operations and the Petal District courthouse, hosting the city's highest-profile trials. Inside, the galleries offer spacious viewing areas and elevated balconies for observing the proceedings, and the holding cells resemble luxury suites compared to other jails in the city.⁠
2120632389:
Nivakta's Crossing

Nivakta's Crossing is a village at the very southern edge of Rostland situated on the northern bank of the Shrike River and overlooking the Stolen Lands of the River Kingdoms to its south.⁠
2124303899:
Zom Kullan

Zom Kullan, the capital city of Nagajor, is located inside a volcano deep in the Kullan Dei mountain range. The volcano Zom Kullan is built around is still active and it is believed that it is only through rituals conducted by the royal naga queen, First Mother Vassath Shethagri and her naga royal family that stop the volcano's fury and prevent its eruption.⁠
2127952709:
Ilizmagorti

The city of Ilizmagorti (pronounced ihl-izz-mah-GOR-tee)⁠ is the only settlement of any size on Mediogalti Island.⁠

Known to its foes as Scum Tide City, and to its friends as the Black Pearl of the Tropics, the city's exact location is unlikely to appear on any map thanks to the efforts of the Red Mantis to remove it from all records. Many of the ships that dock in the harbour are pirates, but the port is also used by a number of (comparatively) honest merchant vessels.

The population is also assumed to include a large number of Red Mantis assassins, which means a certain wariness is probably advisable when dealing with strangers.⁠
2131060149:
Candlemere Tower

Candlemere Tower is a tower sacred to the cult of Yog-Sothoth, located in the Stolen Lands of the River Kingdoms. It has the power to open portals between planets if the correct rituals are performed on the night of the winter solstice. Recently, the investigator Olun Shandus, after learning of the tower's existence from a copy of the Pnakotic Manuscripts, travelled to Candlemere with a small group of companions, but their ritual proved faulty, depositing them on a world long consumed by bholes and allowing the bholes to burrow into the Stolen Lands.⁠
2133660279:
Krega

Krega is a small town on the western edge of the Estrovian Forest in the nation of Mendev that acts as a stop on the crusade route between the port city of Egede to the east and the front of the Worldwound to the west. Because the Fourth Mendevian Crusade attracts warriors from all over the Inner Sea region, Krega has a diverse population, most of whom work to supply the crusaders with anything they might need, from weapons and armor to food, shelter, and more earthly pleasures.⁠⁠
